correctness.rationale: For integer k and s, the normalized slice Fourier transform has Laplace transform (1-e^{-z})^n times a rational function. Its inverse transforms vanish at positive integers for distinct simple poles, while exactly one double pole contributes A*m and no simple residue, where A is a nonzero explicit product. An alternating binomial identity gives the exact coefficient. Counting union of pair-collision hyperplanes (single intersections of codimension one, multiple intersections codimension at least two) proves the sharp leading term. The proof handles all n>=5, 2<=s<=n-2 and frequency boxes; 552 exact and 11 independent-method numerical tests corroborate it. Unspecified higher-multiplicity Fourier coefficients are not asserted.

value.rationale: The object is a canonical family of cube hyperplane sections and uniform-matroid polytopes. For all nontrivial n>=5 hypersimplices, a natural Fourier-support invariant has sharp codimension-one growth independent of slice level, and the amplitudes obey a nontrivial common binomial law at every generic resonance. These relations hold across unbounded dimension and slice parameters and identify exact structure beyond an arbitrary numerical instance. The deeper multiple-collision classification is expressly unproved and not needed for this sharp leading invariant.
